# ambercast

> Prompt-native end-to-end testing.

## START HERE
- [Introduction](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/introduction/): Understand ambercast's prompt-driven workflow, generating deterministic test plans and grounding artifacts that replay with 0 AI calls and repair deliberate UI drift.
- [Philosophy](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/philosophy/): Explains the durable rationale and architectural principles behind ambercast.

## TUTORIALS
- [Your first test in 5 minutes](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/tutorials/quick-start/): Guide your first generated test from prompt creation through generation, replay, and review.
- [Reading your first plan and grounding](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/tutorials/review-your-first-plan/): Learn how to locate generated plan and grounding files and check their freshness.
- [Healing a test after a UI change](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/tutorials/repair-your-first-drift/): Repair an existing ambercast test on a disposable practice application after a locator-affecting UI change by configuring idempotent replay isolation.
- [Running ambercast in GitHub Actions](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/tutorials/github-actions/): Set up a portable GitHub Actions workflow to run ambercast with check and run commands.

## HOW-TO GUIDES
- [Write effective prompts](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/how-to/write-effective-prompts/): Author focused test prompts with clear outcomes and verify plan generation with a dry run.
- [Manage secrets](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/how-to/manage-secrets/): Follow the safe authoring path to declare secrets in prompts and resolve them from environment variables.
- [Configure targets](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/how-to/configure-targets/): Configure targets, replay isolation, and secret sink origins in ambercast.
- [Choose an AI provider](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/how-to/choose-ai-provider/): Configure ambercast to use Claude, Codex, or automatic provider resolution for test generation.
- [Select which tests run](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/how-to/select-tests/): Selection recipes to choose which test prompts run.
- [Control grounding write-back](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/how-to/control-grounding-writeback/): Configure how Ambercast writes back changed grounding caches locally and in CI.
- [Review generated diffs](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/how-to/review-generated-diffs/): Follow a practical review order to inspect generated diffs across prompts and their companion files.
- [Manage artifacts in git](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/how-to/manage-artifacts-in-git/): Configure git tracking and ignore rules for ambercast plan, grounding, and run artifacts.
- [Run on other CI platforms](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/how-to/run-on-other-ci/): Portable CI recipes for GitLab and generic runners.
- [Recover stale artifacts](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/how-to/recover-stale-artifacts/): Resolve stale, missing, or orphaned artifacts based on their check status.
- [Upgrade between versions](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/how-to/upgrade/): Release-safety procedure for upgrading ambercast and regenerating stale plans.
- [Troubleshoot common failures](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/how-to/troubleshoot/): Look up troubleshooting actions by observed symptoms to resolve ambercast failures.
- [Contribute](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/how-to/contribute/): Repository contribution recipe for submitting changes and reporting vulnerabilities.

## REFERENCE
- [Configuration](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/reference/configuration/): Configuration keys and resolution rules for ambercast.
- [Prompt file format](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/reference/prompt-format/): Exact file identity, normalization rules, secret grant extraction, and secret reference syntax for ambercast test prompts.
- [Discovery patterns](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/reference/discovery-patterns/): Configured test file discovery matching rules, pattern grammar, and ordering.
- [Reports](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/reference/reports/): Reference for ambercast structured report schemas, envelope properties, command result shapes, and error structures.
- [Error codes](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/reference/error-codes/): Reference vocabulary of stable error codes, execution scopes, and exit codes for ambercast.
- [Exit codes](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/reference/exit-codes/): Process exit codes and aggregation priority for machine-facing status in ambercast.
- [Environment variables](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/reference/environment-variables/): Exhaustive reference of environment variables read by Ambercast and the filtering boundary for AI-provider child processes.
- [File layout](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/reference/file-layout/): Reference for Ambercast path arithmetic, artifact producers, timing, and implementation-backed repository policies.
- [JSON Schemas](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/reference/json-schemas/): Publication contract and inventory of generated JSON Schemas for Ambercast configuration, plan, grounding, and report artifacts.
- [Compatibility](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/reference/compatibility/): Artifact-format compatibility across package versions and provenance-driven regeneration rules for plans, groundings, and reports.
- [Changelog](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/reference/changelog/): User-visible product behavior and public-contract changes across ambercast releases, with breaking changes listed first.
- [Security policy](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/reference/security-policy/): Supported versions and vulnerability reporting procedures for ambercast.
- [Glossary](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/reference/glossary/): Normative site-wide terminology and index of literal translation-invariant tokens for Ambercast.

### CLI
- [CLI overview](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/reference/cli/overview/): Reference for parser-wide CLI behavior, command-flag dispatch, and discovery defaults in ambercast.
- [ambercast generate](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/reference/cli/generate/): Reference for ambercast generate flags, provider executor resolution, companion file artifacts, and exit statuses.
- [ambercast run](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/reference/cli/run/): Reference for the ambercast run command, covering CLI flags, replay paths, AI provider fallback, cache-only execution, grounding write-back, and report persistence.
- [ambercast check](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/reference/cli/check/): Inspect the freshness and validity of Ambercast test plans and grounding artifacts from the CLI.
- [ambercast heal](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/reference/cli/heal/): Command-line reference for ambercast heal, defining flags, repair execution boundaries, authorization, and side effects.

## PLAN SPECIFICATION
- [Ambercast Plan Specification](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/spec/overview/): This specification describes the artifacts accepted by ambercast 0.3.1.
- [Plan document](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/spec/plan-document/): `PlanDocument` is a strict object.
- [Steps](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/spec/steps/): Every committed step is a strict branch of `Step`, discriminated by `kind`; every branch has `id: StepId`.
- [Value types](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/spec/value-types/): All other chapters MUST use these definitions rather than restating their shapes.
- [Grounding document](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/spec/grounding-document/): `GroundingDocument` is a strict object bound to exactly one Plan digest.
- [Element fingerprint](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/spec/fingerprint/): `Fingerprint.
- [Freshness and digests](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/spec/freshness/): `inputsDigest` MUST be lowercase SHA-256 of canonical JSON for a freshly constructed object with exactly these five members: `normalizedTestMd`, `schemaVersion`, `generatorPromptTemplateFingerprint`, `planProducerBundleFingerprint`, and `targetDefinitions`.
- [Canonical JSON](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/spec/canonical-json/): Digest inputs MUST use compact RFC 8785-compatible JSON encoded as UTF-8, with no inter-token whitespace.
- [Secrets in plans](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/spec/secrets/): Plans MUST represent secret values only with Value types `SecretRef`; the contiguous `{{secrets.
- [Conformance](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/spec/conformance/): Ambercast's publication pipeline MUST derive Plan, Grounding, configuration, and report JSON Schema from the Zod runtime schemas, not maintain a hand-written parallel schema.
- [Specification changelog](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/spec/changelog/): Artifact version acceptance MUST follow Ambercast Plan Specification, not release-number intuition.

## EXPLANATION
- [Plan lifecycle and freshness](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/explanation/plan-lifecycle/): Understand artifact provenance, plan freshness decisions, and grounding companion bindings when evaluating whether an artifact can be replayed.
- [Replay and grounding](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/explanation/replay-and-grounding/): Explain replay paths and their safety boundary.
- [Healing model](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/explanation/healing-model/): Understand bounded escalation and human control in ambercast's self-healing workflow.
- [Trust and security](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/explanation/trust-and-security/): Trust boundaries and fail-closed architectural choices across plan validation, page observations, evidence collection, and secret handling.
- [Determinism in CI](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/explanation/determinism-in-ci/): Explains the trust boundaries and structural isolation governing Ambercast execution in CI environments.
- [How ambercast compares](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/explanation/comparison/): A comparison of ambercast's design model with code generation, record-and-replay frameworks, and direct-driving agents.
- [Status and roadmap](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/explanation/status-and-roadmap/): Track the implemented command boundary of ambercast 0.3.1, planned capabilities, and the pre-1.0 version policy.

## FOR AI AGENTS
- [Using ambercast from an AI agent](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/agents/overview/): Operational reading order and bounded execution loop for AI agents using ambercast.
- [Operating contract](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/agents/operating-contract/): Action boundaries, command preconditions, prohibitions, and next safe actions for invoking ambercast commands.
- [Setup prompt](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/agents/setup-prompt/): Complete copy-pasteable operating prompt providing a thin, review-first boundary for an agent working on a requested test.
- [Reading structured output](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/agents/reading-structured-output/): Branch on the report envelope, inspect reportPersistence and errors, and evaluate command-specific result statuses in ambercast.
- [Machine-readable resources](https://kotarotsubaki.github.io/ambercast/agents/machine-readable-resources/): Published machine-readable documentation artifacts and their availability rules for AI agents.
